chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Back from the army: Jose Curbelo starts his band at La Conga
summary: On discharge Machito returned to La Conga, where Curbelo had become a bandleader with a similar instrumentation but a different style.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Okay, all right. We are in 1943, we are moving in 1944, you got out of the army. What happened when you got out, Macho?

Well, I come back to La Conga at the - Jose Curbelo a new manager, a manager and he sold the name that he acquired, La Conga, because La Conga was like a show-case of the Latin music, so he went to Miami, went to different places in New York because there was an opening. The Cuban music was crazy, everybody was crazy about Conga, Cha-cha-cha, you name it, everything that we played, they eat 'em up.
Okay, in other words, Jose Curbelo officially got started......
...and the idea came while he was a member of your band while he was filling-in for Varona.....
....or was he a band leader before that?
No, he was a band leader before that, but he organized his band....
...right there, right there. He just became a band leader at La Conga.
Do you know how many men he started with?
Well, he started with one trumpet, three saxes, the same combination that we had, the only thing that his trumpet player didn't double with saxophone.
Do you remember any of the numbers in his repertoire?
He had a lot of numbers that was similar to us and his father, the late Curbelo, he was a composer and he was the bass player of the band and he had a good repertoire.
Okay. At any time did you feel that he was a rival?
No, because it was a different style.
